section_summary: The section opens with the end of an assessment of Japan’s war production, labor, shipping, and logistical vulnerabilities, followed by a confidential account of conditions observed in Japan by tea merchant A. T. Hellyer in 1941. Most pages contain a May 1943 Chungking Embassy despatch and its enclosure of economic reports drawn from Japanese and Nanking-regime broadcasts. The reports cover mobilization plans, transport, industry, food, finance, and administration across Japan and Japanese-occupied territories.

subfiles.title: Assessment of Japanese Economic and Military Production
subfiles.about: An assessment of Japan’s labor, aircraft production, shipping, and strategic vulnerabilities.
subfiles.summary: The concluding pages estimate limits on labor transfers and aircraft production. They identify shipping and concentrated industrial capacity as vulnerabilities while noting the logistical difficulty of supplying Allied forces in China.

subfiles.title: Current Conditions Existing in Japan
subfiles.about: Tea merchant A. T. Hellyer describes conditions observed during a 1941 visit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hellyer reports surveillance of Americans, scarce labor and gasoline, price controls, military activity, and depressed merchant morale. He also describes his tea business, agricultural conditions, and his belief that Japan wished to avoid war with the United States.

subfiles.title: Economic Material from Japanese Broadcasts
subfiles.from: George Atcheson Jr., U.S. Embassy, Chungking
subfiles.about: The Embassy forwards economic reports from Japanese broadcasts for the Board of Economic Warfare.
subfiles.summary: Forwards a fuller enclosure supplementing Embassy telegram 718 on broadcasts monitored from April 30 to May 9, 1943.

subfiles.title: Economic Items Selected from Japanese and Nanking-Regime Radio Broadcasts
subfiles.doc_type: despatch enclosure with table of contents
subfiles.to: Department of State; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: A monitored and translated collection of economic reports from Japan and Japanese-occupied areas.
subfiles.summary: The enclosure begins with a table of contents and reports on Japan’s 1943–44 mobilization plans for materials, production, power, labor, and transportation. Further items describe resource development, food supply, finance, shipping, communications, and administrative measures in Japan, Manchuria, occupied China, Hong Kong, Southeast Asia, and Thailand. The text continues beyond page 512.
